source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST v2 insert → checkAndSetData → DataType_FloatVector case → json.Unmarshal([]byte(dataString), &vectorArray) → json.Unmarshal handles both array and string-encoded array → converts to []float32
source_grounding.note: Source code reveals vector field handling uses json.Unmarshal which inherently handles multiple JSON representations: direct arrays [0.1,0.2] and string-encoded arrays '[0.1,0.2]'. The standard library json.Unmarshal function parses both correctly to []float32.

cognition_match.developer_quote: REST v2 API fails to properly serialize/deserialize complex data types - Returns wrong values for large integers, Array fields in raw protobuf format, AutoId not working for Int64 PK
cognition_match.note: Filed under REST v2 data type handling, but vector string parsing via json.Unmarshal works correctly and handles both formats by design

verdicts.rationale: The claimed defect (vector as string rejected in insert) is FALSE_POSITIVE. Source code analysis reveals vector field handling uses json.Unmarshal which inherently accepts both direct arrays and string-encoded arrays. Live reproduction confirms insert with vector='[0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4]' succeeds and subsequent search returns correct results. The json.Unmarshal standard library function correctly parses JSON arrays regardless of whether they're direct values or string-encoded.
